newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Creditanstalt Hungary's profit, mkt share up in 96.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt Hungary's profit, mkt share up in 96.

text.p: The Hungarian unit of Austria's Creditanstalt Bankverein on Thursday reported rising profits for 1996 and said a continued expansion in 1996 resulted in higher market share.
Matthias Kunsch, Creditanstalt's general manager for Hungary, also said the bank had enough capital to finance further expansion plans, which included the adding of six branches to the current 14.
"Our capital adequacy ratio was almost 20 percent (in 1996), we are very comfortably supplied with capital," Kunsch said at a news conference.
"Our capital gives a basis for that growth this year and in the coming years should not be limited due to lack of capital."
The bank released its audited IAS results on Thursday and said it boosted its after-tax profit to 2.37 billion forints in 1996 from 2.04 billion in 1995.
The bank's net interest income grew to 5.40 billion forints in 1996 from 3.50 billion in 1995, while its net fee revenues soared to 824.1 million forints from 122.5 million.

The bank's balance sheet total grew to 116.12 billion forints at the end of 1996 from 76.98 billion in 1995, according to which Creditanstalt was the eighth biggest bank in Hungary last year in a ranking which excluded data of ING Bank, which does not make such information public.
In a statement, Creditanstalt said it boosted its market share to around 2.7 percent in 1996 from 2.2 percent in 1995, "helped by the expansion of its branch network."
Kunsch, referring to data of the state financial and capital market supervision APTF, added that the bank's overall market share was now above three percent.
The bank boosted its corporate lendings by 30 percent in 1996, which gave it a market share of nearly four percent in this area.
"We regard this (30 percent) as a good result if we take into consideration the ample liquidity we experienced in the Hungarian money market and in the corporate sector," Kunsch said.
The bank maintained its conservative lending policy, Kunsch said, adding that Creditanstalt's provisions fell to below one percent of the its loan portfolio.

Answering a question about how Creditanstalt's takeover by Bank Austria would influence the bank's operations in Hungary, Kunsch said talks will start soon to avoid competition in this country where Bank Austria has a 50 percent stake in Europai Kereskedelmi Bank Rt, a smaller commercial bank.
